html:
The Uqair Protocol was an agreement made at the port of Uqair in December 1922 that set the borders between the Najd of Ibn Saud, Kuwait and British-run Iraq.

The British official Percy Cox drew the lines himself on a map. He gave Ibn Saud a large stretch of land that Kuwait claimed, about two thirds of it by most accounts, and in return gave Iraq land claimed by Ibn Saud. Two neutral zones were left where Bedouin could graze freely.

The lines ignored tribal ranges, as desert borders had never existed before. Oil was later found under the neutral zones, which were divided in the 1960s and 1970s. Kuwaitis long resented the protocol, made without them at the table after the Battle of Jahra.
sum: The Uqair Protocol was an agreement made at the port of Uqair in December 1922 that set the borders between the Najd of Ibn Saud, Kuwait and British-run Iraq.
